newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Perpetual Trustees sees yr net rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Perpetual Trustees sees yr net rise.

text.p: Perpetual Trustees Australia Ltd said on Monday it expected a rise in 1996/97 net profit, but not as large as the 29 percent increase achieved in 1995/96.

"It is too early in the 1996/97 financial year to provide any forecasts," chairman John Lamble said in the company's annual report. "It is sufficient to say that we have budgeted for a further increase in profit, though not at the same rate of increase as last year," Lamble said.
Australia's largest trustee company reported a 1995/96 net profit of A$14.56 million, 29.4 percent above the 1994/95 result of A$11.25 million.
"In the year ahead, we aim to further improve our profit performance with a particular focus on growing our revenues," managing director Graham Bradley said in the report.
"In a competitive marketplace, and faced with a generally subdued business outlook, this task will pose a signficant challenge for the group," Bradley said.

Of Perpetual's three main divisions, the corporate and institutional services unit raised 1995/96 sales by 34.7 percent to A$31.9 million followed by private clients with a 33.1 percent rise to A$30.4 million and the funds management arm by 26.3 percent to A$24.2 million. - Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
